content.text: Scene 1
Scene 1
(Setting: inside the circle of covered wagons. LEONORA sits near the campfire. Nearby, adults and children are cooking over the fire and hanging clothes to dry. HENRY sits down next to LEONORA.)
HENRY: Did today feel really long to you?
LEONORA: Yes! We probably walked fifteen miles today. And my father said we still have over five hundred miles to go.
HENRY: You mean we're barely over halfway there?
(HENRY and LEONORA both laugh, shaking their heads.)
LEONORA: At least that makes it easy to sleep on this hard ground.
HENRY: (picking at his sleeve and looking away from LEONORA) It should. But I haven't been sleeping.
LEONORA: Why not?
HENRY: Well…my dad has been talking about the new life we'll have in Oregon. But all I can think about is our old farm in Missouri. How can we move somewhere we've never seen? What if it's a mistake?
LEONORA: (after thinking for a moment) Have you ever heard of constellations?
HENRY: Constellations?
LEONORA: Constellations are those groups of stars that look like people or animals. You can look up to the sky and see something familiar, even if you're somewhere new. That's nice, isn't it?
HENRY: Yeah, I guess. Are there constellations here?
LEONORA: Yep!
(LEONORA and HENRY walk away from the fire and look at the sky.)
LEONORA: (pointing to stars in the sky) You see that really bright star and the bright stars next to it—the ones that look like they form a pan?
HENRY: Yeah, I see it!
LEONORA: That's the Big Dipper. It's part of another constellation called Ursa Major, which means "big bear."
HENRY: Really? How do I find that one?

LEONORA: Look—that first bright star is the end of the tail. And if you keep going from the front of the pan, you can see another bright star that makes the bear's nose. (LEONORA traces a line in the sky.) You can even find the stars that make the feet. (LEONORA points at different points in the sky.)
HENRY: I see it! It's just like a bear in Missouri! Will I still be able to see it when we get to Oregon?
LEONORA: (smiling) You sure will.
(LEONORA and HENRY continue to talk and point at the sky.)

Scene 2
(Setting: inside the circle of wagons, very early morning. LEONORA, HENRY, and other people are sleeping under blankets on the ground.)
(A YOUNG MAN plays a song on a bugle. LEONORA and the other people begin to stir and get up. LEONORA notices that HENRY is still asleep.)
LEONORA: (shaking HENRY) Henry! Wake up!
HENRY: (rubbing his eyes and stretching) Oh. Did I miss the morning call?
LEONORA: Seems like you finally got some sleep.
HENRY: (slowly) I did. I even had a dream.
LEONORA: What was it about?
HENRY: (tossing his blanket aside and jumping up from the ground) It was about Oregon. It was like I could see it clearly!
LEONORA: (smiling) What did it look like?
HENRY: There was this beautiful farm that we built ourselves. We had chickens, and cattle, and gardens full of vegetables. We even lived near a river. Our old farm in Missouri didn't have a river.
LEONORA: Soon we'll see if your dream was right! Let's pack up our blankets and get some breakfast.

content.text: Scene 1
Scene 1
(Setting: the flight deck. NANA is piloting the spaceship. ELVIN and WILFRED run in.)
ELVIN: (shouting) Nana! Wilfred is going crazy!
(WILFRED is making beeping noises, and his lights are blinking.)
WILFRED: Sizzling stars, I'm having a heart attack!
NANA: Calm down, Wilfred. Robots can't have heart attacks. Looks like you're just picking up an asteroid storm.
(WILFRED's blinks get faster, and his beeps get louder.)
ELVIN: That's so cool! I've never been in an asteroid storm!
WILFRED: We're ruined!

NANA: We're already late delivering our cargo to Planet Volg. There's no time to make a detour around the storm, so we'll need to go straight through. Strap yourselves in—it's going to be a bumpy ride!
WILFRED: (still blinking and beeping) We'll be crushed to space dust!
ELVIN: I'll save us. I never get hit by asteroids when I play Space Avengers 3000!
NANA: Computer games aren't real life. But you can help by checking the ship's pressure system while I steer.
(The spaceship screen shows dozens of huge, lumpy-looking rocks that seem to be rushing toward the ship. At the controls, NANA zigzags around them.)
WILFRED: Bewildering boulders! It's the end of the world!
(WILFRED's blinking lights all flash at once. His beeps turn into a siren.)
NANA: There's a planet down there. Brace yourselves for landing!
Scene 2
Scene 2
(Setting: a meadow with S-shaped plants and rocks on Planet Orba. NANA uses tools to fix a spaceship engine. ELVIN reads WILFRED'S control screen.)
NANA: Boy, that landing really did a number on this engine. I hope I can fix it.
ELVIN: It's a good thing nothing happened to Wilfred's radar. It says we're on Planet Orba.
WILFRED: (suddenly pointing at the S-shaped rocks) Oh no! Rattlesnakes! Their bite is poisonous to humans!
ELVIN: I think your info-chip got damaged in the landing, Wilfred. Those are rocks, not snakes!
NANA: Well, I could use a snake right now to get inside this engine. There's a button that has to be pushed, but my tools won't reach it. If the button stays stuck, we can't leave.
(Something long and wiggly appears from behind one of the rocks.)
WILFRED: (beeping wildly) SNAKE!!
(ORPS pokes his head over the rock. His long, skinny arms wave.)
ORPS: Greetings! I'm Orps, president of Orba.
ELVIN: (whispering to WILFRED) It's a space creature, but its arms do look like snakes.
NANA: (saluting ORPS) I'm Commander Pickering of Spaceship Aries. This is my grandson, Elvin, and our robot, Wilfred. We had to make an emergency landing, and we damaged our engine.
ORPS: Perhaps we can fix it.
WILFRED: (whispering to ELVIN) Even his fingers look like snakes!
(ELVIN smiles, and his eyes light up. He points to ORPS's fingers.)
ELVIN: Actually, President Orps, it looks like your finger might be just the tool we need.
ORPS: Really?
NANA: (nodding) Elvin's right. There's a button that's stuck, and none of my tools can reach it. You might be able to hit it.
ORPS: Sounds good. Let's go for it.
(ORPS lets NANA guide his finger into the engine. A loud popping sound is heard.)
ORPS: (surprised) Oh my! What was that?
NANA: (grinning) That was the button popping up. Our engine is fixed! Thank you!
ELVIN: Woohoo! (speaking quietly to NANA and ORPS) Now we should head off to Planet Volg before Wilfred starts thinking these trees look like snakes.
WILFRED: (screaming) Did I just hear there are snakes in the trees? Someone help us!
(NANA, ELVIN, and ORPS laugh.)

content.text: Scene 1
Scene 1
(Setting: the flight deck. NANA is piloting the spaceship. ELVIN and WILFRED run in.)
ELVIN: (shouting) Nana! Wilfred is going crazy!
(WILFRED is making beeping noises, and his lights are blinking.)
WILFRED: Sizzling stars, I'm having a heart attack!
NANA: Calm down, Wilfred. Robots can't have heart attacks. Looks like you're just picking up an asteroid storm.
(WILFRED's blinks get faster, and his beeps get louder.)
ELVIN: That's so cool! I've never been in an asteroid storm!
WILFRED: We're ruined!

NANA: We're already late delivering our cargo to Planet Volg. There's no time to make a detour around the storm, so we'll need to go straight through. Strap yourselves in—it's going to be a bumpy ride!
WILFRED: (still blinking and beeping) We'll be crushed to space dust!
ELVIN: I'll save us. I never get hit by asteroids when I play Space Avengers 3000!
NANA: Computer games aren't real life. But you can help by checking the ship's pressure system while I steer.
(The spaceship screen shows dozens of huge, lumpy-looking rocks that seem to be rushing toward the ship. At the controls, NANA zigzags around them.)
WILFRED: Bewildering boulders! It's the end of the world!
(WILFRED's blinking lights all flash at once. His beeps turn into a siren.)
NANA: There's a planet down there. Brace yourselves for landing!
Scene 2
Scene 2
(Setting: a meadow with S-shaped plants and rocks on Planet Orba. NANA uses tools to fix a spaceship engine. ELVIN reads WILFRED'S control screen.)
NANA: Boy, that landing really did a number on this engine. I hope I can fix it.
ELVIN: It's a good thing nothing happened to Wilfred's radar. It says we're on Planet Orba.
WILFRED: (suddenly pointing at the S-shaped rocks) Oh no! Rattlesnakes! Their bite is poisonous to humans!
ELVIN: I think your info-chip got damaged in the landing, Wilfred. Those are rocks, not snakes!
NANA: Well, I could use a snake right now to get inside this engine. There's a button that has to be pushed, but my tools won't reach it. If the button stays stuck, we can't leave.
(Something long and wiggly appears from behind one of the rocks.)
WILFRED: (beeping wildly) SNAKE!!
(ORPS pokes his head over the rock. His long, skinny arms wave.)
ORPS: Greetings! I'm Orps, president of Orba.
ELVIN: (whispering to WILFRED) It's a space creature, but its arms do look like snakes.
NANA: (saluting ORPS) I'm Commander Pickering of Spaceship Aries. This is my grandson, Elvin, and our robot, Wilfred. We had to make an emergency landing, and we damaged our engine.
ORPS: Perhaps we can fix it.
WILFRED: (whispering to ELVIN) Even his fingers look like snakes!
(ELVIN smiles, and his eyes light up. He points to ORPS's fingers.)
ELVIN: Actually, President Orps, it looks like your finger might be just the tool we need.
ORPS: Really?
NANA: (nodding) Elvin's right. There's a button that's stuck, and none of my tools can reach it. You might be able to hit it.
ORPS: Sounds good. Let's go for it.
(ORPS lets NANA guide his finger into the engine. A loud popping sound is heard.)
ORPS: (surprised) Oh my! What was that?
NANA: (grinning) That was the button popping up. Our engine is fixed! Thank you!
ELVIN: Woohoo! (speaking quietly to NANA and ORPS) Now we should head off to Planet Volg before Wilfred starts thinking these trees look like snakes.
WILFRED: (screaming) Did I just hear there are snakes in the trees? Someone help us!
(NANA, ELVIN, and ORPS laugh.)

content.text: PROPS:

elements.text: Props for Scene 1: a screwdriver, a hammer, and a homemade time machine. The time machine is a large cardboard box with a large hole cut out of it. Holiday lights, flashlights, broken antennae, and various old buttons are attached with gray duct tape. Inside are two seats with seat belts. There is a control panel made up of buttons and screens.

content.text: Scene 1
Scene 1

(Setting: the basement. ELI is using the tools to adjust different things on his cardboard-box invention. He carefully checks every inch of the invention as he works. JADE stands nearby, watching ELI.)
JADE: (sighing and tapping her foot) Eli, are you almost done?
ELI: Almost! I just need to tighten a few screws.
(There is a loud pop followed by a lot of beeping noises. Lights and buttons attached to the cardboard box light up.)
JADE: Wow. That's actually kind of cool, Eli! So…is that it? Can we go outside now?
ELI: (opening a cardboard door for JADE) Of course that's not it! It's a time machine. We have to try it out!
(JADE rolls her eyes and steps into the cardboard box. ELI follows her, and they sit down in the seats.)
JADE: I don't know what you think is going to happen. It's neat that you made it light up and everything, but—
(ELI begins to push buttons. Different lights flash on the machine, faster and faster. A quiet whirring sound gets louder and louder.)
JADE: Eli? Eli! What's going on?
ELI: (laughing excitedly as he watches the various screens and buttons) Buckle up, Jade!
(The lights flash brighter and faster, and the whirring sound hits its highest volume. Suddenly, there is a loud popping sound, and the machine goes dark.)
JADE: Eli?
Scene 2
Scene 2
(Setting: a tropical jungle. JADE and ELI are sitting in the time machine.)
JADE: (clutching the armrests of her seat tightly and staring at Eli) Eli?
ELI: (grinning and excitedly flipping through his notebook) If I've calculated right, we're in the same place. We're just in a totally different year.
JADE: But…how do we get back home?

ELI: Don't worry about that! This big red button will always take us back home. I designed the machine so that it only lets us watch what happens around us. That way, we don't accidentally change something about the past…or the future. No one else can see us or the time machine. How cool is that?
JADE: I guess. But what year are we in?
ELI: Well, I'm still fine-tuning that part, so I'm not exactly sure. There are a number of possible dates—
(A screech and a distant roar are heard. The ground rumbles with giant footsteps.)
JADE: (slowly) Is one of them a date way, way in the past? A date when there would be dinosaurs?
ELI: (nodding and smiling) That sounds right! Are you ready to explore?
(ELI and JADE exit the time machine. More screeches and sounds from the jungle animals are heard. ELI and JADE look around in wonder as they begin to explore.)
